name: תַּחַת
gloss: place, (one) in place of another; or beneath
summary: Three men in the genealogies of Chronicles: a Kohathite Levite, son of Assir, of the line of Korah from which Heman the singer came (1Ch 6:9, 22), and two Ephraimites, father and grandson, in the line of Shuthelah (1Ch 7:20). A station of Israel in the wilderness bears the same name (Num 33:26–27). The name is the word תַּחַת itself, whose senses are "beneath", "(one's) place" and "in place of"; scripture does not say which the name means. Seth was named as a son given "in place of Abel" (Gen 4:25), which shows how a child could be thought of as given in another's place, but no verse ties that thought to this name.

evidence.note: "Assir his son, Tahath (תַּחַת) his son, Uriel his son" (with 6:8).
In Heman's line: "son of Tahath, son of Assir, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah".
"Bered his son, and Tahath his son, and Eleadah his son, and Tahath his son": two Ephraimites of the name.
The same name for a wilderness station: "they camped at Tahath".
תַּחַת in a naming: Seth, "another seed in place of Abel"; a parallel only, not this name's explanation.
The sense "place": "remain every man in his place (תַּחְתָּיו)".

note: TIPNR keys use English versification: Tahath@1Ch.6.24 is the Levite of Hebrew 1Ch 6:9 and 6:22 (English 6:24, 6:37). The place Tahath (Num 33:26–27) is not a person and is not tagged. BDB's key w.an.ad also catches the preposition by spelling, so its token count (291) far exceeds the six uses of the name; the word sheet should still show this entry only on the name. The meaning is left open between the word's senses; no source explains the name.
